description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy performance of six methods across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 3 to 3000, with tick labels at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80% with a tick label interval of 5. The black line representing 'Base' starts at around 60% at a co-occurrence number of 3 and increases to approximately 67% at 3000. The blue line for 'FT' begins at around 61% and rises to about 69% across the same range. The red line for 'IKE' starts at approximately 65% and reaches around 70% at 3000. The brown line representing 'MEND' begins at about 66% and increases to roughly 75% at 3000. The purple line for 'MEMIT' starts at around 66% and rises to approximately 74% across the range. The green line for 'ROME' begins at about 72% and reaches around 78% at 3000.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
